title: CLI argument boundaries are lost when constructing the shell command
reasoning: Only the prompt is shell-quoted before the argument list is joined with spaces. Binary paths, model values, and extra_args therefore lose their argument boundaries when they contain whitespace, and shell metacharacters can be interpreted as executable syntax. A configured binary path containing spaces or an extra argument containing a literal space cannot be passed reliably.
reproduction: Configure binary as '/opt/Gemini CLI/bin/gemini', or pass an extra_args element containing spaces. The generated command splits that single value into multiple shell words.
recommendation: Build an unquoted argument vector and apply shlex.join once at the shell boundary, removing the existing prompt-only quoting; alternatively pass the vector directly if the runtime supports it.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No tests were included demonstrating preservation of CLI arguments through shell serialization.
suggestedRegressionTest: Verify argument round-tripping for prompts, binary paths, model values, and extra arguments containing spaces, quotes, dollar signs, and shell metacharacters.
minimumFixScope: GeminiAgent._build_command, command serialization, and argument-boundary tests.

history.reasoning: The original path and lines still exist. Current agent.py:655-678 builds raw arguments and serializes them once with shlex.join, supporting the intended repair. tests/agent_runner/agents/gemini_agent_test.py:636-661 covers round-tripping binary paths, models, prompts, and extra arguments containing spaces, quotes, and shell metacharacters. No linked patch attempts were supplied. Targeted pytest validation exited 1 before collection because the read-only environment provides no usable temporary directory, so the repair cannot be reported as verified fixed.

history.note: Verified raw argv serialization preserves CLI argument boundaries; 284 adapter tests pass.
